The holder of an enclosure permit to enclose a Crown road or Crown watercourse is taken to be the owner or lessee (as the case requires) of the land enclosed for the purposes of any law relating to dividing fences.

heading.b: Certain gates erected under this Division to be treated as public gates

block.txt: A gate is a public gate for the purposes of the Roads Act 1993 if—
the Minister directed the erection of the gate under this Division, and
the gate is erected in accordance with the direction, and
the Minister has, in the direction, specified that the gate, when erected, is to be a public gate for the purposes of the Roads Act 1993.
In this Division—
easement includes an easement without a dominant tenement referred to in section 88A of the Conveyancing Act 1919.
holder, in relation to Crown land, means—
a person who holds a lease under this Act over the land, or
a person who is a mortgagee of a lease under this Act over the land.
The Minister may grant an easement over Crown land on any terms and conditions that the Minister thinks appropriate (including terms and conditions relating to compensation payable to the Crown).
The benefit of an easement granted under this section may be annexed to land even if, at the time the easement is granted, the land is vested in the Crown.
An easement granted under this section is not extinguished because the land with the benefit or burden of the easement becomes, or both become, vested in the Crown.
Sections 88A and 181A of the Conveyancing Act 1919 apply to a notice or instrument purporting to grant an easement for the purposes of this section.
Section 89 of the Conveyancing Act 1919 applies to an easement granted for the purposes of this section.

heading.b: Consent of holders generally required for creation or release of easement

block.txt: When granting or releasing an easement over land under this Division, the Minister must be satisfied that—
for the grant of an easement—the holder (if any) for the time being of the land has consented to the creation of the easement, or
for the release of an easement—the holder (if any) for the time being of the land having the benefit of the easement has consented to the release of the easement.
A failure to comply with subsection (1) does not affect the validity of any easement or release.
This section does not apply to easements granted under section 5.49.

heading.b: When consent of holder not required for creation of easement over Crown land

block.txt: The Minister may grant an easement over Crown land without the consent of the holder (if any) for the time being of the land for any of the following purposes—
to enable the owner of other land to access the owner’s land,
to enable necessary services (for example, drainage, water, gas or electricity services) to be provided to other land,
to enable a person who has access rights over the land (including for the purpose of travelling stock) to continue to have access to the land when the land is sold,
to preserve or protect the interests or rights of the Crown in the land (including forestry or mining rights) when the land is sold.
The Minister may create an easement for a purpose under subsection (1) if the Minister is satisfied that—
for a purpose under subsection (1) (b)—the easement would enable the owner of the other land to avoid unreasonable expenses involved in obtaining alternative service provision, or
Subsection (2) does not apply to an easement being created—
in connection with the sale of the land to the holder of a lease over the land, or
for a purpose under subsection (1) (d).

Despite anything in the Real Property Act 1900, an easement granted under this section over Crown land in the Western Division can be registered under that Act without the need for a plan of survey for the easement.

It is sufficient if an easement registered as permitted by subsection (4) is registered by reference to boundaries shown diagrammatically on a compiled easement plan of a kind approved by the Registrar-General.

heading.b: Local councils to seek easements from Crown in certain cases

block.txt: This section applies to a local council that has an ongoing need to enter Crown land to carry out work of the kind referred to in section 191A (Power of entry—construction and maintenance of water supply, sewerage and stormwater drainage works) of the Local Government Act 1993.

The local council must, as soon as practicable after becoming aware that it needs access on an ongoing basis, ask the Minister to create an easement for access to the Crown land to carry out the work it needs to carry out.
The local council must provide the Minister with any information that the Minister requires concerning the proposed easement (including the work it needs to carry out).
Without limiting section 5.47, the Minister must grant the easement if the Minister is satisfied that it is appropriate to do so.
This section does not limit the powers of a local council under section 191A of the Local Government Act 1993.

heading.b: Creation of easements for public access

block.txt: An easement for public access may be granted—
for Crown land proposed to be sold under this Act—by the Minister at any time before the sale, or
for dedicated or reserved Crown land—by the Minister, or
for Crown land authorised to be sold or transferred by the Minister under another Act—by the Minister at any time before the sale or transfer, or
for land under a lease from the Crown—by the Minister with the consent of the holder of the lease, or
for freehold land—by its owner.
An easement for public access may be granted for the benefit of the Crown without a dominant tenement.
An easement for public access may be defined by reference to a natural or physical feature as it exists from time to time.

An easement for public access over land confers on the public a right to enter the land and to carry on any activity except an activity of a kind prescribed by the regulations (a prescribed activity).
A person must not carry on a prescribed activity on land that is subject to an easement for public access.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.
This section extends to Crown land regardless of whether or not—
there is a holding or enclosure permit over it, or
it is dedicated or reserved Crown land.

heading.b: Rights of owners or lessees of land affected by public access easements

block.txt: An owner or lessee of land over which there is an easement for public access cannot erect any structure unless the Minister gives written consent for it.
Despite subsection (1), the Minister’s written consent is not required to erect—
a fence or gate that does not unduly hinder public entry to the land, or
any other kind of structure prescribed by the regulations.
Division 9.3 applies in respect of structures erected on land that is subject to an easement for public access in the same way as it applies in respect of structures erected on Crown land.
An owner or lessee who suffers damage caused by a person using an easement for public access contrary to this Act or the regulations may recover damages from the person.

heading.b: Release of easements benefiting Crown land

block.txt: The Minister may at any time release any easement that benefits Crown land.
This Division does not affect any right of any other person to release an easement granted under this Division.

heading.b: Method for granting or releasing easements under this Division

block.txt: An easement granted under this Division may be granted—
for land to which the Real Property Act 1900 applies—in the way provided in that Act or in section 88B of the Conveyancing Act 1919, or
for land to which the Real Property Act 1900 does not apply—
in the way provided in section 88B of the Conveyancing Act 1919, or
by notice published in the Gazette (except if it is an easement for public access).
An easement benefiting Crown land may be released by the Minister under this Division—
for land to which the Real Property Act 1900 applies—in accordance with that Act, or
for land to which the Real Property Act 1900 does not apply—by notice published in the Gazette.

heading.b: Recording of particulars of easement or release in Register

block.txt: This section applies if an easement over land to which the Real Property Act 1900 applies is granted or released under this Division.

The Registrar-General may record any particulars of the grant or release of the easement as the Registrar-General considers necessary in any folio of the Register for the land that, in the Registrar-General’s opinion, is affected by the grant or release.

heading.b: Imposition of restrictions and covenants on Crown land

block.txt: The Minister may, on behalf of the Crown, impose any restrictions on use, or public positive covenants, on Crown land.

The restriction or public positive covenant is to be imposed in accordance with section 88D or 88E of the Conveyancing Act 1919 (as appropriate), and that Act applies in respect of the restriction or public positive covenant.
See also section 13.4, which applies in relation to a restriction on use or public positive covenant imposed as referred to in this section.
Without limiting subsection (1), a restriction or public positive covenant extends to any separate lots created by a subsequent subdivision of the land to which the restriction or covenant relates.
The Minister may, on behalf of the Crown, exercise the functions of a prescribed authority under sections 88D and 88E of the Conveyancing Act 1919 in relation to the restriction or covenant.

Section 88D (9) of the Conveyancing Act 1919 does not apply in respect of any interest in the land acquired by the purchaser of the land before the restriction or public positive covenant takes effect and, accordingly, does not prevent the enforcement of the restriction or covenant. A reference in this subsection to a purchaser includes a reference to a mortgagee (or a person claiming through a mortgagee) or any other person claiming through the purchaser.
This section does not limit the Minister’s power under Division 5.4 to include conditions in a contract of sale of Crown land.

heading.b: Removal of restrictions or covenants on Crown land

block.txt: The Minister may consent to the removal of a restriction or covenant on Crown land imposed under this Division.

Division 2 of Part 2 of Schedule 7 provides for restrictions on use, and public positive covenants, on Crown land imposed under the Crown Lands Act 1989 to continue in effect under this Act. Accordingly, they can be removed under the provisions of this Act (including this section).
Where the restriction or covenant was originally imposed under Part 4A of the Crown Lands Act 1989, the Minister must consent to its removal if—
the land is being sold or an application to purchase the land under a purchasable lease is granted, and
the purchaser or applicant requests its removal and provides the Minister with any documentation required by the Minister to give effect to its removal.

However, the Minister cannot consent to the removal of a restriction or covenant on Crown land originally imposed under Part 4A of the Crown Lands Act 1989 without the consent of the Minister for the Environment if the land—
adjoins or abuts, or is within 100 metres of, land dedicated or reserved under the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974, or
is within, or comprises or contains, or is part of, or adjoins or abuts, or is within 100 metres of—
a wilderness area (as defined in the Wilderness Act 1987), or
land for the time being identified as wilderness under that Act.

Also, the Minister cannot consent to the removal of a restriction or covenant on Crown land originally imposed under section 77B of the Crown Lands Act 1989 unless satisfied, having regard to the prescribed assessment principles, that it is appropriate to do so.

The regulations may make provision for or with respect to principles (the prescribed assessment principles) to be applied by the Minister when deciding whether it is appropriate to consent to the removal of a restriction or covenant on Crown land originally imposed under section 77B of the Crown Lands Act 1989.

The Minister is not to recommend to the Governor the making of a regulation that provides for or amends the prescribed assessment principles unless the Minister has certified that the Office of Environment and Heritage was consulted about the principles or amendment.

Except as provided by subsections (2), (3) and (4), this section does not limit the circumstances in which the Minister may decide to remove (or consent to the removal of) a restriction or covenant on Crown land.
In this section—
Crown land includes former Crown land.

heading.b: Forestry rights and carbon related rights

block.txt: The Minister may, on any terms and conditions determined by the Minister, grant a forestry right over Crown land.

Section 1.5 (1) defines a forestry right to have the same meaning as in section 87A of the Conveyancing Act 1919. Section 87A of that Act defines a forestry right to include a carbon sequestration right in relation to land. Carbon sequestration is the process by which a tree or forest absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
A forestry right is, for all purposes, taken to be a profit à prendre (see section 88AB of the Conveyancing Act 1919).
Before doing so, the Minister must be satisfied that any holder of a lease over the Crown land has consented to the grant of the forestry right.

If the Crown land is dedicated or reserved Crown land, the provisions of section 2.18 apply to the granting by the Minister of a forestry right over the land as if it were a relevant interest under that section.
If the Crown land is under a perpetual lease, the Minister may, on any terms and conditions determined by the Minister, consent to the holder of the lease granting a forestry right over the land.

The holder of a perpetual lease over Crown land may, with the consent of the Minister under subsection (4), grant a forestry right over the land subject to any terms and conditions determined by the Minister.
Also, the Minister must consult the Minister administering the Forestry Act 2012 before—
granting a forestry right over Crown-timber land (as defined in the Forestry Act 2012), or
consenting to the holder of a perpetual lease over Crown-timber land granting a forestry right.
In the case of Crown-timber land that is a State forest or timber reserve, it is the Forestry Corporation that may grant a forestry right in respect of the land.
Without limitation, the terms and conditions determined by the Minister under this section for the grant of a forestry right may include any restrictions on dealings with the right.

heading.b: Method for granting forestry rights and use restrictions and covenants

block.txt: A forestry right granted under this Division may be created—
for land to which the Real Property Act 1900 applies—in the way provided in that Act or section 88B of the Conveyancing Act 1919, or
for land to which the Real Property Act 1900 does not apply—in any of the following ways—
in the way provided in section 88B of the Conveyancing Act 1919, or
if the Minister consents to it, by an instrument registered in the General Register of Deeds, or
by a notice published in the Gazette (except for a forestry right granted by the holder of a perpetual lease).

Without limiting Division 4 of Part 6 of the Conveyancing Act 1919, restrictions on the use of land and covenants may be imposed in accordance with that Division on Crown land over which a forestry right is granted under this Division.

The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the granting and effect of rights over Crown land in connection with any scheme (whether of this State, the Commonwealth or internationally) for the reduction of carbon emissions or other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

This section, or any regulation made for the purposes of this section, does not limit the granting of forestry rights under this Division that comprise or include carbon sequestration rights (as defined in section 87A of the Conveyancing Act 1919).

heading.b: Payment of royalties, security deposits, fees or other amounts for holdings

block.txt: A holding over Crown land may be granted subject to the payment of any royalty, security deposit, fee or other amount that the Minister may determine in respect of the holding.
Part 6 also provides for rent to be payable on holdings (except incomplete purchases).
The provisions of a holding may include provisions for the determination or redetermination of any royalty, fee or other amount.
The Minister may, from time to time, review the amount of a royalty, security deposit, fee or other amount payable for a holding.
The Minister may, by written notice served on the holder of a holding, change the amount of a royalty, security deposit, fee or other amount payable for the holding.
In this section—
holding does not include an incomplete purchase.

heading.b: Use of land for filming projects

block.txt: Subject to section 5.25, the holder of a holding may, with the Minister’s written consent, grant another person one of the following (a subholding) to enable the person to use the land under the holding to carry out a filming project—
if the holding is a lease—a sublease or licence,
if the holding is a licence—a sublicence.
The Minister may also grant a licence over Crown land (including leased land) under section 5.21.
A subholding granted with the Minister’s consent is subject to any conditions that the Minister thinks fit to impose.
Subsection (1) does not require the consent of the Minister if the use of the land for the purpose of a filming project—
is authorised by the holding or generally consistent with the purposes for which the land may be used under the holding, and
will not affect any native title rights and interests in relation to the land.
If a subholding is granted without the Minister’s consent, it is taken to be a condition of the holding that—
the holder must give the Minister written notice of the grant of the subholding within 28 days after it is granted, and
the holder must ensure that—
the fee charged for the subholding reflects the holder’s costs and is kept to a minimum, and
the subholding requires the film makers when filming to comply with any appropriate safety measures and operational requirements of a kind required by the Minister from time to time.
The Minister may give consent under subsection (1), and the subholding may be granted following that consent, despite any provision to the contrary in the holding or this Act.

heading.b: Crown land acquired by purchase or exchange provides fee simple

block.txt: A person acquiring Crown land by purchase or exchange under this Act obtains an estate in fee simple in the land.
This section does not apply to a person acquiring land under a lease from the Crown by exchange.
The Minister may inform the Registrar-General that a covenant, condition, reservation or provision no longer applies to a holding or land if the Minister is satisfied of it.
The Registrar-General may amend the Register in accordance with that information.
This Part provides for the payment of rent for holdings (including enclosure permits, but not incomplete purchases). It includes provisions for the payment of minimum annual rent for a holding.
If the provisions of a holding provide for how rent is to be determined, redetermined or adjusted, it must be done in accordance with those provisions.
However, if the holding does not provide for how rent is to be determined, redetermined or adjusted, this Part will enable it to be done as follows—
when determining rent on granting or renewing a holding—the Minister,
when redetermining or adjusting rent for a holding during its term—the Secretary.
Generally speaking, this will be done by reference to certain principles (including the principle that market rent should be payable).

Schedules 1–4 contain special provisions concerning continued holdings, land in the Western Division and purchasable leases. Section 1.13 provides that those provisions prevail over the provisions of this Part to the extent of any inconsistency.
In this Part—
during the term of a holding, in relation to a holding with no term (such as a perpetual lease), includes while the holding remains in force.
holding includes an enclosure permit, but not an incomplete purchase.

heading.b: Rent is generally payable for holding

block.txt: The holder of a holding is required to pay rent for the holding unless—
the provisions of the holding provide for no rent to be payable, or
the rent has been waived or its payment postponed under this Act.
Section 12.15 enables the Minister to—
waive, reduce, or remit rent for a holding, or
postpone the payment of rent for a holding, or
grant a rebate of rent for a holding.
A holding may include provisions concerning the amount of rent payable for the holding (including how it is to be determined, redetermined or adjusted and when and to whom it is payable).
The rent payable for a holding is to be determined, redetermined or adjusted—
for a holding that includes provisions for how rent is to be determined, redetermined or adjusted—in accordance with those provisions, or
in any other case—in accordance with the provisions of this Part and any other applicable provisions of this Act or the regulations.

Subsection (3) (a) does not limit the powers of the Secretary to redetermine or adjust rent if a provision of this Act or the regulations requires or permits the Secretary to redetermine or adjust rent following a change to the area, purposes or conditions of the holding (for example, under section 4.3 and Divisions 7.2 and 7.3).
The Minister is responsible for determining the rent payable for a holding when it is granted or renewed.
The Secretary is responsible for redetermining or adjusting the rent for a holding during the term of the holding if a provision of this Act or the holding requires or permits it to be done.

The Secretary is to redetermine or adjust the rent for a holding during the term of the holding in accordance with the provisions of this Part unless the provisions of the holding provide differently.

A provision of a holding (whether granted before or after the commencement of this Part) that provides for the Minister to redetermine or adjust its rent is to be read in all cases (including for the purposes of subsection (2)) as providing for the Secretary to do it instead of the Minister.

heading.b: Annual rent cannot generally be less than minimum rent

block.txt: The annual rent for a holding is not to be less than the minimum rent as at the date the rent is due and payable.
If the annual rent for a holding on a due date is less than the minimum rent as at that due date, the annual rent is increased to the minimum rent.
Despite subsection (1), the holder of a holding is not required to pay the minimum rent if—
the holder has been granted a waiver, reduction, remission, postponement or rebate of rent resulting in no rent or a lesser amount of rent being payable, or
the provisions of the holding provide that the holder is not required to pay the minimum rent.
The minimum rent of a holding at each due date is to be calculated using the following formula—
M is the minimum rent.
B is the minimum base rent.
C is the Consumer Price Index number for the last quarter for which a number was published before the due date for the rent.
D is the Consumer Price Index number for the last quarter for which a number was published before the rent base adjustment date.
In this section—
minimum base rent means $472 or any greater amount that may be prescribed by the regulations.

rent base adjustment date means 1 July first occurring after the commencement of this section or, if the minimum rent base is prescribed by the regulations, the date prescribed by the regulations as the rent base adjustment date.

heading.b: Determination, redetermination and adjustment of rents
General principles for rent determinations or redeterminations

block.txt: The principles set out in this section are to be applied when—
determining the rent for a holding (including when determining provisions concerning rent for inclusion in the provisions of holding), and
redetermining the rent for a holding.
The following principles apply to the determination or redetermination of rent for a holding—
the rent is to be the market rent for the land under the holding having regard to any restrictions, conditions or terms to which it is subject,
regard may be had to any additional value that, because of the holding, has accrued (or may reasonably be expected to accrue) to other land held by the holder of the holding,
regard may be had to the duration of the time for which the rent will be payable.
The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, exempt a specified holding (or class of holding) from the market value principle set out in subsection (2) (a) if—
the Secretary has recommended the making of the order, and
the Treasurer has agreed to the exemption.

A recommendation made by the Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal in relation to the rent for a holding (or class of holdings) may be applied by the Minister or Secretary (as the case requires) despite subsection (2) when—
determining or redetermining the rent for any lease or licence to which the recommendation relates, or
determining or redetermining the rent for any enclosure permit to which the recommendation relates.
The rent payable for a holding may be increased during the term of the holding—
if the holding’s provisions specify a methodology for determining increases—in accordance with that methodology, or

if the holding’s provisions provide that the rent is fixed and cannot be changed during the term—in accordance with a redetermination made by the Secretary under this Division, but only where the redetermination is required because—
the area of the holding has changed, or
of a provision of Schedule 1, 2, 3 or 4, or

if the holding’s provisions make no provision about whether or how rent may be increased during the term or provide for the Secretary to make redeterminations of rent under this Act—in accordance with a redetermination made by the Secretary under this Division, or

if a provision of this Act or the regulations requires or permits the Secretary to redetermine rent following a change to the area, purposes or conditions of the holding (for example, under section 4.3 and Divisions 7.2 and 7.3).

The Secretary must (if required), and may (if permitted), redetermine the rent for a holding if a provision of this Act or the regulations requires or permits the Secretary to redetermine rent following a change to the area, purposes or conditions of the holding (for example, under section 4.3 and Divisions 7.2 and 7.3).
The following provisions apply if the Secretary is required or permitted to redetermine the rent for a holding in other circumstances—

subject to paragraphs (b) and (c), the Secretary may redetermine the rent as often as the Secretary considers appropriate or as required by the regulations unless the holding’s provisions provide differently,
the rent must be redetermined at least once every 5 calendar years,
the rent for a holding cannot be redetermined more than once in each calendar year.

The Secretary must give the holder of a holding written notice of any redetermination of rent made by the Secretary. The notice may contain any other information (including in relation to the making of objections) as the Secretary considers it appropriate to include.
The redetermined rent cannot take effect unless the written notice is given.
The holder of a holding may object to a redetermination of rent made by the Secretary unless—
the redetermination is done under the provisions of the holding rather than this Part, or
the provisions of the holding preclude objections against redeterminations, or
the redetermination results from a recommendation of the Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal, or
the redetermination results from an increase in the minimum annual rent payable for the holding.
The objection must—
be made in writing in the approved form, and
contain the approved particulars, and
be lodged with the Secretary within 28 days after the holder is given written notice of the redetermination.
After considering an objection, the Secretary may—
reject the objection, or
vary the redetermined rent to take into account anything raised by the objection that the Secretary considers relevant.
The Secretary must give the objector written notice of the Secretary’s decision concerning the objection (including any adjusted rent resulting from the decision).
In this section—
approved means approved by the Secretary from time to time.

heading.b: Alteration, withdrawal and forfeiture of holdings

block.txt: This Part enables the Minister—
to alter or revoke the conditions or purposes of a holding (or exempt holders of holdings from conditions of the holding), and
to withdraw land from a holding for public purposes, and
to declare that a holding is forfeited for contraventions of provisions of this Act or another Act or the conditions of the holding and for certain other reasons.

Schedules 1–4 contain special provisions concerning continued holdings, land in the Western Division and purchasable leases. Section 1.13 provides that those provisions prevail over the provisions of this Part to the extent of any inconsistency.
In this Part—
altered includes modified or added to.

heading.b: Alterations, revocations and exemptions concerning conditions and other restrictions

block.txt: To avoid doubt, this Division extends to conditions contained in a Crown grant.

heading.b: Alteration or revocation of conditions and purposes

block.txt: The Minister may direct that any of the following be altered or revoked (whether conditionally or unconditionally)—
the conditions attaching to a holding or the land to which a holding relates,
the purpose of a holding.
A direction can only be on the application, or with the consent, of the holder of the holding concerned.

On the application of the holder of a holding, the Minister may exempt (either permanently or temporarily and to a specified extent) the holder from complying with a condition attaching to a holding or the land to which a holding relates.
An exemption may be conditional or unconditional.

heading.b: Rent redetermination following alteration, revocation or exemption

block.txt: If a condition or purpose is altered or revoked (or an exemption from compliance with a condition is given) under this Division, the Secretary may redetermine the rent for a holding for the remainder of the current rent redetermination period applicable to the holding.

heading.b: Removal of conditions and other restrictions

block.txt: The Minister may direct that any covenant, condition, reservation or provision attaching or applying to a holding or the land to which a holding relates ceases to attach or apply to the holding or land.

The Registrar-General must, when requested by the Minister, make recordings in the Register that are necessary to give effect to a direction under this Division of which the Registrar-General has been notified.

heading.b: Withdrawal of land from holding for public purposes

block.txt: The Minister may, by notice published in the Gazette, withdraw land required for a public purpose from any holding.
A withdrawal does not operate to extinguish any debt to the Crown relating to the land withdrawn, except to the extent to which the Minister directs.
The Minister may, by notice published in the Gazette, revoke or modify any withdrawal.
Compensation is payable for the withdrawal of land under this section, but subject to the conditions or provisions applying to the holding concerned.

The provisions of the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991 relating to the payment of compensation for land acquired by compulsory process apply, with any modifications that may be prescribed by the regulations, to the payment of compensation under this section.
On the withdrawal of land from a holding, the Secretary may—

if the rent payable in respect of the holding is subject to periodic redetermination—redetermine the rent and adjust (in proportion to the land withdrawn) any other money payable in respect of the lease or licence, or
if the rent is not subject to periodic redetermination—proportionately adjust—
the rent and any other money payable in respect of the holding, and
if the withdrawal is from a lease—any rent base for the lease.
If part of a rent base apportioned under subsection (6) is less than the minimum rent base, that part of the rent base is increased to the minimum rent base.
Part 6 applies to the redetermination of rent for a holding under this section.
In this section—
minimum rent base means $472 or any other amount that may be prescribed by the regulations.
public purpose includes any of the following—
the purpose of a road,
the purpose of a travelling stock route,
the purpose of a camping reserve or other reserve,
a purpose of a kind prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this definition or specified by a notice published by the Minister in the Gazette.
The Minister may declare that a holding is forfeited if—
the holder contravenes a provision of this Act or another Act applying to, or a condition of, the holding, or
the holder does not make any payment due under this Act, the regulations or a condition of the holding within 3 months after the due date, or
the holder gives up or parts with possession of the whole or any part of the holding except as authorised by or under this Act, the regulations or a condition of the holding, or
the holding becomes subject to forfeiture under this Act.
The acceptance of money by the Crown in respect of a forfeited holding does not operate as a waiver of the forfeiture.
A person (other than the holder of a perpetual lease) cannot seek relief against forfeiture from any court or tribunal in connection with a forfeiture of a holding under this section.
See section 7.13 for the right of the holder of a perpetual lease to appeal to the Land and Environment Court against forfeiture.

heading.b: Forfeiture takes effect when notice given

block.txt: The forfeiture of a holding takes effect—
if the holding is under the Real Property Act 1900—on the Minister causing a notice of the forfeiture to be entered in the Register, or
if the holding is not under the Real Property Act 1900—on notice of the forfeiture being published in the Gazette.
When a holding is forfeited—
the land to which the holding relates (to the extent to which it is not Crown land) becomes Crown land, and
all money paid to the Crown in respect of the holding is forfeited.
See section 1.10 (When land becomes Crown land because of this Act).
Without limiting section 1.10, land that becomes Crown land because of this section is vested free of any estate conveyed by or related to the holding.

The forfeiture of a holding does not operate to release the holder from any obligation to comply with a condition or provision that, by its nature, is required to be complied with after the holding is forfeited.
The Minister may (whether conditionally or unconditionally) reverse a forfeiture of a holding.
The reversal of the forfeiture of a holding takes effect—
if the holding is under the Real Property Act 1900—on the Minister causing a notice of the reversal to be entered in the Register, or
if the holding is not under the Real Property Act 1900—on notice of the reversal being published in the Gazette.
A forfeiture that is reversed is taken never to have had effect.

heading.b: Appeal to Land and Environment Court against forfeiture of perpetual leases

block.txt: The holder of a perpetual lease (but no other holding) may appeal to the Land and Environment Court against any declaration of forfeiture made under this Division.
Subject to any order of the Land and Environment Court, the making of the appeal does not stay the effect of the declaration.

heading.b: Removal of entries in Register about mortgaged leases

block.txt: This section applies if—
a lease of Crown land is forfeited under this Act, and
a mortgage over the lease is registered in the Register.

The Minister may request that the Registrar-General remove both the recording of the lease and the mortgage from the Register if the Minister reasonably considers that the Minister has complied with the provisions of any agreement between the mortgagee and the Minister concerning the forfeiture of the lease.
The Registrar-General must remove the recordings concerned from the Register if the Minister requests it.

heading.b: Forfeited, surrendered or vacant Crown land may be added to adjacent or adjoining holdings

block.txt: The Minister may, by notice published in the Gazette, add any of the following kinds of Crown land to Crown land to which an adjoining or adjacent holding relates—
Crown land that was under a forfeited or surrendered holding,
vacant Crown land.
The Minister can add the Crown land only with the consent of the holder of the adjoining or adjacent holding.
The land is added subject to any conditions that the Minister may determine.

heading.b: Ownership of improvements when holding ends

block.txt: This section applies if a holding ends because it is forfeited, surrendered, terminated or ceases to have force for any other reason.

Except as provided by this section or the terms and conditions of a holding over land, the end of the holding results in all improvements to the land becoming the property of the Crown. Also, no compensation is payable for the improvements.
The Minister may, within 2 years after the holding ends, require the former holder—
to remove any improvement made or owned by the former holder or a previous holder, and
to make good any damage done to the land because of the removal of the improvement (including damage to other improvements that were not required to be removed).
If an improvement is removed by the former holder when required by the Minister, the Crown ceases to have (and is taken never to have had) any right to the improvements.

If a former holder does not comply with a requirement of the Minister to remove an improvement, the Minister may direct any government sector employees, contractors or other agents to enter the land and remove the improvement.
A person directed under subsection (5) to enter land and remove an improvement is authorised to enter the land, at any reasonable time, to remove the improvement.
Subsection (6) does not authorise a person to enter any part of a structure used only for residential purposes except with the consent of the occupier of the structure.

The Minister may recover the cost of removing an improvement and making good any damage to the land (including to other improvements) from the former holder in any court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due by that person to the Crown.
In this section—
improvements to land includes structures in or on the land.
This Part provides for—
the issuing of native title certificates by the Minister, and

the obligations of certain Crown land managers for dedicated or reserved Crown land and local councils vested with Crown land in connection with the management of native title issues in relation to the land (including using native title managers to provide advice on certain dealings with the land), and
compensation responsibilities concerning native title rights and interests for the conduct of these Crown land managers and local councils.
In this Part—
approved training or qualifications means training or qualifications approved under section 8.2.
excluded land means each of the following—
land subject to an approved determination of native title (as defined in the Native Title Act 1993 of the Commonwealth) that has determined that—
all native title rights and interests in relation to the land have been extinguished, or
there are no native title rights and interests in relation to the land,

land where all native title rights and interests in relation to the land have been surrendered under an indigenous land use agreement (as defined in the Native Title Act 1993 of the Commonwealth) registered under that Act,
an area of land to which section 24FA protection (as defined in the Native Title Act 1993 of the Commonwealth) applies,
land where all native title rights and interests in relation to the land have been compulsorily acquired,
land for which a native title certificate is in effect.
relevant land means—
dedicated or reserved Crown land managed by a council manager, or
dedicated or reserved Crown land managed by a non-council manager assigned as a category 1 manager under Division 3.5, or
land vested in a local council under Division 4.2 (Vesting of Crown land in local councils).
responsible person for relevant land means the local council or non-council manager that manages the land or the local council in which the land is vested.

heading.b: Approved training or qualifications for native title managers

block.txt: The Minister may, by notice published in the Gazette, approve kinds of training or qualifications that a person must have to act as a native title manager for the purposes of this Part.

heading.b: Relationship of Part with Local Government Act 1993

block.txt: This Part applies despite anything in the Local Government Act 1993.

The Minister may, at the Minister’s absolute discretion, issue a certificate (a native title certificate) to a person for specified Crown land or former Crown land stating that, following investigations made by the Department, there is adequate evidence to show that native title rights and interests in relation to the land have been extinguished or do not exist.
Section 12.8 enables the Minister to charge fees for services provided by the Department (including in connection with issuing native title certificates).
The Minister may, by notice given to the person to whom a native title certificate is issued, revoke the certificate.
A native title certificate is taken to be revoked if the land becomes subject to an approved determination of native title (as defined in the Native Title Act 1993 of the Commonwealth).
Copies of any native title certificates issued under this section may (but need not) be published on the Department’s website.
Any requirements of the native title legislation in relation to land are not affected by the issuing of a native title certificate for the land.
This Division applies to responsible persons for relevant land, but not if the land is excluded land.

heading.b: Employment or engagement of native title manager

block.txt: A responsible person for relevant land must employ or engage at least one native title manager to ensure the person’s dealings with the land comply with any applicable provisions of the native title legislation.
A native title manager must have approved training or qualifications.

heading.b: When advice of native title manager required

block.txt: A responsible person for relevant land cannot do any of the following unless the person has first obtained the written advice of at least one of the person’s native title managers that it complies with any applicable provisions of the native title legislation—
grant leases, licences, permits, forestry rights, easements or rights of way over the land,
mortgage the land or allow it to be mortgaged,

impose, require or agree to covenants, conditions or other restrictions on use (or remove or release, or agree to remove or release, covenants, conditions or other restrictions on use) in connection with dealings involving the land,
approve (or submit for approval) a plan of management for the land that authorises or permits any of the kinds of dealings referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (c).
However, the written advice of a native title manager is not required for the sale or other disposal of the land.

See also Divisions 3.4 and 3.5 and section 4.9 for limitations on Crown land managers and local councils vested with Crown land to sell or dispose of managed or vested land in relation to which native title rights and interests may or do exist.

heading.b: Notice of native title managers to be given to Minister

block.txt: A responsible person for relevant land must give written notice to the Minister about—
whether any person is engaged or employed as a native title manager for the responsible person, and
the name and contact details of that person.
The notice must be given as soon as practicable after 30 June (but not later than 31 October) of each year.

heading.b: Compulsory acquisition of native title rights and interests requires Ministerial consent

block.txt: This section applies to a responsible person for relevant land, but only if the person is managing the land as Crown land manager.
This section does not apply to a local council that is vested with Crown land under Division 4.2.

The responsible person for relevant land cannot, without the written consent of the Minister, take action that will result in the compulsory acquisition of native title rights and interests in relation to the land.

heading.b: Division does not affect compliance with native title legislation

block.txt: A responsible person for relevant land must comply with any requirements of the native title legislation in relation to the land (including in respect of the matters referred to in sections 8.7 (1) and 8.9).
This Division applies to the following conduct (relevant conduct)—
the conduct of a local council in connection with—
any dedicated or reserved Crown land for which it is or was a Crown land manager, or
any former Crown land that is or was vested in it under Division 4.2 (Vesting of Crown land in local councils),
the conduct of a non-council manager assigned as a category 1 manager under Division 3.5 in connection with any dedicated or reserved Crown land for which the person is or was a Crown land manager.
The State will remain liable for its own conduct.

heading.b: Compensation payable by person engaged in relevant conduct

block.txt: This section applies if—
compensation is payable under section 24JAA, 24KA, 24MD or 24NA of the Native Title Act 1993 of the Commonwealth in respect of an act that is relevant conduct, and
the act is attributable to the State under that Act.

Subject to the regulations, the person who engaged in the relevant conduct is declared, in accordance with section 24JAA (9) (b) (i), 24KA (6) (b) (i), 24MD (4) (b) (i) or 24NA (7) (b) (i) (as the case requires) of the Native Title Act 1993 of the Commonwealth, to be liable to pay the compensation.
The regulations may limit the circumstances or persons (or both) to which the declaration made by subsection (2) applies.

heading.b: Contributions and indemnification for compensation for relevant conduct

block.txt: Without limiting section 8.12, a person who engaged in relevant conduct must (in accordance with the regulations) contribute to, or indemnify the State against, any compensation payable by the State for the impact of the conduct on native title rights and interests.
Any amount payable to the State under this section is recoverable by the State as a debt in a court of competent jurisdiction.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to—
contributions to, or indemnification against, compensation payable by the State for the impact of relevant conduct on native title rights and interests, and

conferring jurisdiction on the Land and Environment Court to resolve disputes between the State and persons who engaged in relevant conduct concerning the allocation of responsibility for the payment of compensation for the impact of the conduct on native title rights and interests.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the following—
the obligations and liabilities of native title managers and responsible persons for relevant land in connection with the administration of this Part or the native title legislation,
compliance with this Part or the native title legislation in connection with relevant land.
This Part contains provisions to ensure that Crown land is protected from damage and improper use. The provisions make it an offence for a person—
to use Crown land for certain purposes, or
to pollute or contaminate Crown land.
The Part enables the Secretary to issue orders to stop unlawful or unsafe activities.
The Part also gives the Minister, authorised officers and Crown land managers certain remediation and enforcement powers (including conferring powers to give directions) to protect Crown land.
In this Part—
damage—
in relation to land includes—
harming an animal, or picking a plant, that is in or on that land, or
damming, diverting or polluting any waters on that land, or
damaging anything in or on the land (for example, a structure or any object or place of cultural value), or
removing anything, or part of anything, in or on the land, and
in relation to a plant, includes picking the plant, and
in relation to an animal, includes harming the animal.
erection, in relation to a structure, includes any work carried out in creating the structure.
interfere, in relation to a substance on, in or forming part of Crown land, includes remove, cut, dig up, disturb, displace, stack and heap the substance.
parking, in relation to water craft, includes the mooring of water craft.
substance, in relation to Crown land, includes plants, trees, timber, turf, stone, clay, shells, earth, sand and gravel.
A person must not do any of the following—
reside on Crown land,
erect a structure on Crown land,
graze stock on Crown land,
drive stock on Crown land,
clear, dig up or cultivate Crown land,
interfere with any substance on, in or forming part of Crown land,
deposit or leave any of the following on Crown land except in a place or receptacle provided for the purpose—
any rubbish or litter, refuse, dead animal or other similar matter,
any matter of a kind prescribed by the regulations,
enclose Crown land (except a road or watercourse to which section 5.36 applies).
Maximum penalty—as determined under section 11.7.
A person must not cause or permit a contravention of subsection (1).
Maximum penalty—as determined under section 11.7.

heading.b: Pollution or contamination involving Crown land

block.txt: A person must not do any of the following—
pollute or contaminate Crown land or any waters in, on or under the land,
pollute or contaminate other land or any waters in, on or under the land if the source of the pollution or contamination is in, on or under Crown land.
Maximum penalty—as determined under section 11.7.
A person must not cause or permit a contravention of subsection (1).
Maximum penalty—as determined under section 11.7.

heading.b: Authorised officers may give directions to stop structure or land use

block.txt: An authorised officer may direct a person, within a specified period, to stop—
using a structure on Crown land that the officer considers is being used without lawful authority, or
carrying on an activity on Crown land of a kind prescribed by the regulations.
A person must not contravene a direction.
Maximum penalty (subsection (2))—

heading.b: Notices prohibiting structure or land use

block.txt: The Minister may cause a notice to be displayed in a conspicuous place on or near Crown land (or at a commonly used access point to the land) that prohibits persons from—
using a structure on the land without lawful authority, or
carrying on an activity on the land of a kind prescribed by the regulations.

A Crown land manager of dedicated or reserved Crown land may cause a notice to be displayed in a conspicuous place on or near the land (or at a commonly used access point to the land) that prohibits persons from carrying on an activity on Crown land of a kind prescribed by the regulations.
A person must not use a structure, or carry on an activity, on Crown land if the person is prohibited from doing so by a notice under this section.
Maximum penalty (subsection (3))—

heading.b: Directions concerning vehicles on Crown land

block.txt: The Minister may give reasonable directions to persons concerning the entry, use and parking or storage of vehicles on Crown land.
A direction under subsection (1) must be given—
by means of a sign displayed in a conspicuous place on or near the Crown land (or at a commonly used access point to the land), or
by any other means as may be prescribed by the regulations.
A person must not interfere with, alter or remove any sign erected or displayed with the authority of the Minister for the purposes of subsection (2).
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.

An authorised officer or Crown land manager may give reasonable directions to persons concerning the entry, use and parking or storage of vehicles on Crown land for the purpose of preventing danger or harm to persons, animals, structures or property.

A direction given under this section does not have effect to the extent that it would operate to derogate from the rights of the holder of a holding over the Crown land unless the direction is given with the holder’s consent.
A person to whom a direction given under this section applies must not contravene the direction.
Maximum penalty (subsection (6))—

heading.b: Unauthorised structures and materials on Crown land

block.txt: In this Division—
unauthorised material means any material (for example, timber, building materials or equipment) brought on to Crown land without lawful authority, except structures or other fixtures.
unauthorised structure on Crown land means—

a structure that, at the time of its erection, was not authorised to be erected by or under the provisions of this Act or another Act (except Part 11 or 12A of the Local Government Act 1919, Part 1 of Chapter 7 of the Local Government Act 1993 or the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979), or
a structure that—

was authorised to be erected or used by or under the provisions of this Act or another Act (except Part 11 or 12A of the Local Government Act 1919, Part 1 of Chapter 7 of the Local Government Act 1993 or the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979), and
is or was required to be removed by or under those provisions at or within a specified time, and
has not been removed as required.

heading.b: Claims concerning authorisation for structure or material

block.txt: The Minister may cause a claim notice to be—
displayed on or adjacent to a structure or material on Crown land that the Minister considers might be an unauthorised structure or material, or
published in a local newspaper or any other newspaper (if any) as the Minister may determine.
A claim notice must state that any of the following persons may give the Minister a written claim statement concerning the structure or material—
a person who claims to have authority to erect, maintain or use the structure or material (or any part of the structure or material),
a person who claims any interest in the structure or material.
A written claim statement must—
be signed by the person who makes it, and
state the basis for the person’s authority—
to erect, maintain or use the structure (or part of the structure) or to bring in or use the material concerned, or
to claim an interest in the structure or material.
Despite any other Act or law, a person cannot make a claim against the Minister or another person concerning a removal under this Division unless—
the person has given the Minister a duly completed written claim statement, and
the statement is given within one month after the display or publication of the claim notice for the structure or material.

heading.b: Removal of unauthorised structures or materials

block.txt: The Minister may cause any unauthorised structure or material (or part of an unauthorised structure or material) on Crown land to be removed, along with its contents.
The Minister may do so by—
giving a direction under this section to a person, or
using government sector employees, contractors or other agents.
The Minister may give a direction to any of the following persons to remove anything referred to in subsection (1) within a specified period—
a person who erected the unauthorised structure or brought the unauthorised material on to the land,

for an unauthorised structure or material for which a claim notice was displayed or published under section 9.8 for at least one month—a person who used the structure or material after the notice was displayed or published and knew (or ought reasonably to have known) that the notice had been displayed or published,
if it is not possible to give a direction to a person referred to in paragraph (a) or (b)—a person who has a holding over the Crown land on which the unauthorised structure or material is located.
A person given a direction under this section must not contravene the direction.
Maximum penalty—
The Minister cannot use government sector employees, contractors or other agents to remove anything under this section unless—

a claim notice for the structure or material was displayed or published under section 9.8 for at least one month and the Minister was not given any written claim statements under that section within that period, or
a person who was given a direction under this section to remove the thing has not complied with the direction within the specified period.
A person used or required to remove anything under this section is authorised to enter Crown land and remove it even if there is a holding over the land.

heading.b: Minister’s powers over removed structure, materials or contents

block.txt: The Minister may cause anything removed under this Division—
to be destroyed, sold or stored, or
to be returned to a person considered by the Minister to be its owner.
The Minister may, on condition that it is removed, sell anything that the Minister can cause to be removed under this Division.
The Minister may recover, as a debt due to the Crown, the expenses incurred in the removal, destruction, sale or storage of anything under this Division from each appropriate debtor for the thing.
An appropriate debtor for anything removed, destroyed, sold or stored under this Division is—

for anything that was (or was part or contents of) an unauthorised structure or material when it was erected or brought on to the land—the person who erected it or brought it on to the land or caused it to be erected or brought on to the land, or

for anything that was (or was part or contents of) an unauthorised structure or material that a person used in contravention of a direction given to the person by an authorised officer under section 9.4—the person given the direction, or

for anything that was (or was part or contents of) an unauthorised structure or material for which a claim notice was displayed or published under section 9.8 for at least one month—a person who used the structure or material after the notice was displayed or published and knew (or ought reasonably to have known) that the notice had been displayed or published, or

for anything that was (or was part or contents of) an unauthorised structure of a kind referred to in paragraph (b) of the definition of unauthorised structure in section 9.7—the person who was required to remove the structure by or under the provisions set out in that paragraph.
Expenses recoverable by the Minister under this section from 2 or more appropriate debtors are recoverable from all of them jointly and each of them severally.

heading.b: Removal of persons from Crown land
Removal of trespassers from Crown land

block.txt: An authorised officer may apply to the Local Court for an order (a trespasser order) authorising the officer to deal with a person as a trespasser of specified Crown land.
Part 4 of the Local Court Act 2007 applies to proceedings under this section. See section 44 of that Act.

The Local Court may make a trespasser order against a person if the Court is satisfied that the person is unlawfully occupying or using the Crown land (including if the person claims that the occupation or use is authorised under a holding that has expired or been forfeited).
A trespasser order must specify—
the person against whom it is made, and
the Crown land to which it applies, and
the date on which the order takes effect, and
the authorised officer authorised to deal with the person as a trespasser of the Crown land.

If the Local Court makes a trespasser order against a person in relation to Crown land, the order authorises the authorised officer named by the order to enter the land and do any or all of the following—
remove the person from it,
remove any structures or goods from the land that were erected or brought on to the land by the person,
take possession of the land on behalf of the Crown.

Without limiting section 10.15, a person may be removed from Crown land under subsection (4) by an authorised officer with the aid of any other authorised officers or police officers as the authorised officer considers necessary and with the use of reasonable force.
This section applies to the following persons (an authorised person) in relation to particular dedicated or reserved Crown land that is managed by a Crown land manager—
an authorised officer who is an employee of the Crown land manager,
any other employee of the Crown land manager who is authorised in writing by the manager to exercise functions under this section,
if the Ministerial Corporation is the Crown land manager—a person authorised in writing by the Ministerial Corporation to exercise functions under this section.
An authorised person may remove a person from the dedicated or reserved Crown land if the authorised person is satisfied, on reasonable grounds, that—
the person is contravening a provision of the regulations made for the purposes of section 9.25, or
the person’s disorderly conduct is causing inconvenience to persons on the land or entering or leaving it.
A person may be removed from dedicated or reserved Crown land under this section with the assistance of a police officer.

heading.b: Authorised officer may give remediation notice

block.txt: An authorised officer may, by notice given to a person (a remediation notice), require the person to carry out specified remediation work on Crown land within a period specified in the notice.

Before doing so, the authorised officer must be satisfied that the Crown land (or any habitat, plant or animal in or on the land) has been damaged in, or as a result of, the commission of an offence against this Act or the regulations by the person.
A remediation notice may be given regardless of whether proceedings for the offence have been brought or the person has been convicted of the offence.
A remediation notice may be varied or revoked in a further written notice given to the person.
In this section—
damaged includes contaminated.
The remediation work specified in a remediation notice may include one or more of the following types of work—
work to control, abate or mitigate the damage to the land, habitat, plant or animal concerned,
work to maintain, remediate or restore the damaged land, habitat, plant or animal concerned (including replacing dead or removed plants or animals).

heading.b: Minister may authorise certain other persons to carry out remediation work in non-compliance cases

block.txt: If a person does not comply with a remediation notice, the Minister may authorise government sector employees, contractors or other agents to enter the land concerned and carry out all or part of the specified work.
The Minister may recover the cost of that work from the person given the remediation notice in any court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due by that person to the Crown.

heading.b: Entry to land to carry out remediation work

block.txt: A person is authorised to enter land, at any reasonable time, to carry out remediation work required under this Division.
This section does not authorise a person to enter any part of a structure used only for residential purposes except with the consent of the occupier of the structure.
In this Division—
activity includes the use of Crown land (or a structure located on Crown land).
emergency has the same meaning as in the State Emergency and Rescue Management Act 1989.

heading.b: Secretary may issue order to stop unsafe activities

block.txt: The Secretary may, by written notice given to a person, order a person not to carry out a specified activity if the Secretary is satisfied that—
the activity is being carried out on Crown land in a manner that poses a threat to public safety or the environment, or
the activity has become unsafe for the time being because of an emergency.
A person must comply with an order under this section given to the person.
Maximum penalty (subsection (2))—

heading.b: Secretary may issue order to stop unlawful activities

block.txt: The Secretary may, by written notice given to a person, order a person not to carry out a specified activity if the Secretary is satisfied that—
the person is contravening, or is about to contravene, this Act or the regulations because of the activity, or
the activity is being carried out on Crown land without lawful authority.
A person must comply with an order under this section given to the person.
Maximum penalty (subsection (2))—

heading.b: Content and duration of stop activity orders

block.txt: An order under this Division—
takes effect immediately or on any later day that may be specified in the notice, and
is subject to any conditions that the Secretary may specify in the notice.
The Secretary may vary or revoke the order or the conditions of the order in a further written notice given to the person.
An order remains in force until whichever of the following happens first—
the order is revoked by the Secretary,
the period (if any) for which the order is expressed in the notice to be in force ends,
the period of 6 months from the day on which the order took effect ends.

heading.b: Appeals to Land and Environment Court

block.txt: A person may appeal to the Land and Environment Court against a direction, notice or order under section 9.4, 9.9 (2) (a), 9.13 or 9.19 within 28 days (or such other period as is prescribed instead by the regulations) after being given the direction, notice or order.

The lodging of an appeal does not, except to the extent that the Land and Environment Court otherwise directs in relation to the appeal, operate to stay the direction, notice or order appealed against.

It is a defence to the prosecution of an offence against this Part (except Division 9.6) if the defendant proves that there was lawful authority for the conduct or activity that is alleged to give rise to the offence.
A direction under this Part may be given orally or in writing.

Written confirmation of a direction that is given orally is to be given to the person to whom it applies within 7 days after the oral direction is given, unless the oral direction has already been complied with.
This section does not affect the meaning of any provisions of this Act (except for this Part).
For the Public Spaces (Unattended Property) Act 2021, the Minister is the occupier of vacant Crown land.
An authorised officer may exercise any power conferred on the Minister by the operation of this section.
An authorised officer may, on behalf of the Minister, take proceedings for the trespass committed on the vacant Crown land by animals impounded by virtue of this section.
For the purposes of subsection (3), the Minister is taken to be in exclusive possession of vacant Crown land.
This section does not—
prevent a court attendance notice being filed for an offence against section 9.2 or 9.3, or
affect any proceedings for the offence.

heading.b: Regulations concerning care, control and management of Crown land

block.txt: The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the care, control and management of Crown land.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision for or with respect to the following—
the use and enjoyment of Crown land,
the regulation or prevention of the taking of alcohol or other intoxicants on to, and their consumption on, Crown land,
the taking of animals on to Crown land,
the parking and use of vehicles on Crown land and camping on Crown land (including charges for these activities),
the preservation, protection and removal of vegetation, animals, material or substances on Crown land,
charges or fees for entry to, or use of, Crown land,
the closure of Crown land to members of the public and other persons,
the carrying out of commercial activities on Crown land,
the appointment, removal and functions of rangers for Crown land,
the measures to be taken by way of compensation to former holders of exclusive rights of burial in the event those rights are revoked.
Subsection (2) (j) and (k) and this subsection are repealed on a day to be appointed by proclamation.
In this section—
animal includes a bird, reptile or fish.
This Part provides powers to enable the investigation of compliance with this Act, the regulations and the provisions of holdings. It enables the following—
the Minister to appoint authorised officers,
the Minister and authorised officers to obtain information and records,
authorised officers to enter and search non-residential land or structures (and to obtain search warrants to enter and search residential land or structures),
authorised officers to question and identify persons,
authorised officers to seize vehicles used in connection with certain offences.
The Part also creates offences for—
contravening certain requirements made of persons under this Part, or
knowingly engaging in false or misleading conduct in trying to comply with a requirement of this Part, or
obstructing or impersonating an authorised officer.
In this Part—
land use restriction means—
a restriction on use imposed on land under Division 5.10, or
a public positive covenant imposed on land under Division 5.10, or
a condition on land to which a recording under section 5.11 (4) (a), 5.12 (1) (a) or 5.13 (a) relates.

heading.b: When functions are exercised for a compliance purpose under Part

block.txt: A function is exercised for a compliance purpose for the purposes of this Part if it is exercised for the purpose of—
determining whether there has been compliance with or a contravention of this Act or the regulations or any notice, direction, order or requirement issued or made under this Act, or
determining whether there has been compliance with or a contravention of the terms and conditions of a holding, or
determining whether there has been compliance with or a contravention of a land use restriction, or
obtaining information or records for purposes connected with the administration of this Act, or
generally for administering this Act.

heading.b: Offence: contravention of requirement under Part

block.txt: A person must comply with a requirement made of the person under this Part.
Maximum penalty (subject to section 10.25 (4))—
It is a defence to the prosecution of an offence against this section if the defendant proves that there was a lawful excuse for the conduct that is alleged to give rise to the offence.

heading.b: Offence: false or misleading conduct under Part

block.txt: A person must not provide any information or do any other thing in purported compliance with a requirement made under this Part, knowing that it is false or misleading in a material respect.
Maximum penalty—

heading.b: Offences: obstruction or impersonation of authorised officer

block.txt: A person must not—
threaten, hinder, obstruct or delay an authorised officer in the exercise of the officer’s functions under this Act or the regulations, or
damage, destroy or interfere with any vehicle or equipment that is used in the exercise of an authorised officer’s functions under this Act or the regulations, or
impersonate an authorised officer.
Maximum penalty (subject to section 10.25 (4))—
The Minister may, by written instrument, appoint—
a specified qualified person to be an authorised officer, or
persons of a specified class of qualified persons to be authorised officers.
A person is a qualified person for appointment as an authorised officer if the person is any of the following—
an employee of a government sector agency,
an employee of a local council,
an employee of a Crown land manager of dedicated or reserved Crown land,
any other person of a class prescribed by the regulations.
A person cannot be appointed as an authorised officer unless the person has undergone training, or has any competency, that may be required by the Minister.
The Minister may exercise any power conferred by or under this Act on an authorised officer.
Accordingly, in this Act (except this Division and section 10.12) references to an authorised officer include references to the Minister.

heading.b: Exercise of functions by authorised officers

block.txt: An authorised officer has the functions conferred on authorised officers by or under this Act or another Act.
The Minister may, in the instrument of appointment of an authorised officer—
provide that the officer may not exercise specified functions, or
provide that the officer may exercise specified functions only, or

restrict in other ways the functions that the officer may exercise, including (for example) by limiting the circumstances in which the officer may exercise any functions conferred or imposed on the officer.
The Minister must issue an authorised officer with an identity card.
The identity card must—
be in the form approved by the Minister, and
state the following—
that it is issued under this Act,
the name of the authorised officer,
the expiry date (if any) for the appointment.
The identity card may, but need not, contain a photograph of the authorised officer.
An authorised officer must not exercise a function conferred by or under this Act unless an identity card has been issued to the officer by the Minister.
An authorised officer must produce the officer’s identity card for inspection on request when exercising the officer’s functions.
A person who has been issued with an identity card must return it to the Minister (or the Minister’s delegate) on demand.
Maximum penalty (subsection (6)): 100 penalty units.

The Minister may enter into an arrangement with the head of any government agency, or with a local council, for an employee of the government agency or council to exercise the functions of an authorised officer under this Act.

An employee of a government agency or local council who exercises the functions of an authorised officer in accordance with the arrangement is taken to be an authorised officer for the purposes of this Act.

heading.b: Powers to require information or records

block.txt: This Division applies whether or not a power of entry under Division 10.5 is being or has been exercised.

heading.b: Requirement to provide information and records to Minister

block.txt: The Minister may, by written notice given to a person, require the person to provide the Minister with the information or records (or both) for a compliance purpose as the Minister requires in the notice.

heading.b: Requirement to provide information and records to authorised officer

block.txt: An authorised officer may, by written notice given to a person, require the person to provide the authorised officer with the information or records (or both) for a compliance purpose as the authorised officer requires in the notice.

heading.b: Matters to be specified by notice

block.txt: A notice under this Division must specify the manner in which information or records are required to be provided and a reasonable time by which the information or records are required to be provided.
A notice under this Division may only require a person to provide existing records that are in the person’s possession or that are within the person’s power to obtain lawfully.
The person to whom any record is provided under this Division may take copies of it.

If any record required to be provided under this Division is in electronic, mechanical or other form, the notice requires the record to be provided in written form, unless the notice provides differently.

heading.b: Powers of entry and search of land and structures
Powers of authorised officers to enter land and structures

block.txt: An authorised officer may, for a compliance purpose, enter—
any Crown land (or any structure in or on Crown land), and
any land that is not Crown land (or any structure in or on the land), but is subject to a land use restriction, and
any other land (or any structure in or on the land) to gain access to any land or structure referred to in paragraph (a) or (b).
Entry may be—
if the authorised officer reasonably suspects that an offence is being committed on the land—at any time, or
in any other case—at any reasonable time.
The power to enter authorises entry by foot or by means of a vehicle or in any other manner.
Entry may be effected by an authorised officer with the aid of any other authorised officers or police officers as the authorised officer considers necessary and with the use of reasonable force.
This section does not limit the circumstances in which entry may be effected to any land (or any structure in or on land) with the authority of a search warrant under section 10.18.

heading.b: Entry into residential premises only with permission or warrant

block.txt: This Part does not empower an authorised officer to enter any part of a structure used only for residential purposes without—
the permission of the occupier, or
the authority of a search warrant under section 10.18.

heading.b: Powers of authorised officers to do things on entry

block.txt: An authorised officer may, on or in any land (or structure) lawfully entered under section 10.15 (1) (a) or (b), do anything that in the opinion of the authorised officer is necessary to be done for a compliance purpose, including (but not limited to) the things specified in subsection (2).
An authorised officer may do any or all of the following—
examine and inspect any structure, vehicle or other article,
take and remove samples,
make any examinations, inquiries and tests that the authorised officer considers necessary,
take any photographs, films, audio, video and other recordings that the authorised officer considers necessary,
require records to be produced for inspection,
examine and inspect any records,
copy any records,
seize anything that the authorised officer has reasonable grounds for believing is connected with an offence against this Act or the regulations,

for the purposes of paragraph (h), direct the occupier of the land or structure where the thing is seized to retain it on the land or at the structure or at another place under the control of the occupier,
do any other thing the authorised officer is empowered to do under this Part.
The power to seize anything connected with an offence includes a power to seize—
a thing with respect to which the offence has been committed, and
a thing that will afford evidence of the commission of the offence, and
a thing that was used for the purpose of committing the offence.
A reference to an offence includes a reference to an offence that there are reasonable grounds for believing has been committed.
An authorised officer may apply to a warrants issuing officer for the issue of a search warrant if the authorised officer believes on reasonable grounds that—
a provision of this Act or the regulations is being or has been contravened at any premises, or
there is in or on any premises any matter or a thing that is connected with an offence against this Act or the regulations.
